gitCommit.subject: fix(results): stop sharing is undoable, not a browser confirm() (u1we) (#327)
gitCommit.body:
fix(results): stop sharing is undoable, not a browser confirm() (u1we) (#327)

SharePanel handed its only destructive decision to window.confirm() — the one
place in the app that defers to browser chrome. It is unstyleable (ignores
DESIGN.md and both themes), cannot obey TONE.md, and blocks the main thread.

The bead assumed the fix needed a Dialog primitive the repo doesn't have. It
doesn't need one — and it doesn't need a dialog at all.

Revoking a share is a SOFT status flip (ShareController.revokeShare sets
status:"revoked"; the row and its token survive), and PATCH already accepts
status:"active". So stopping a share is genuinely reversible, and Undo restores
THE SAME TOKEN — the link the person already sent works again. That is what makes
an undo honest here rather than a new-link lie; it is also why no "are you sure?"
is warranted. TONE commitment 4 is unpressured and forgiving: a modal bracing for
a mistake is not this app's voice. The app already answers this shape elsewhere
(set-aside's inline reveal→confirm, session-undo's persistent Undo notice) — this
now matches.

The Undo notice is persistent and NOT on a timer. A countdown would be exactly the
pressure TONE forbids.

Also fixes a latent bug found while writing the test: findByResult returns EVERY
share for a result, revoked ones included, so after a reload a revoked share still
rendered with Copy/Preview — offering a link that silently 404s whoever it was
sent to (viewSharedResult rejects a non-active status). The panel now renders only
active shares.

No new component, no new dependency, no <dialog>. Net: the confirm() is gone and
the panel got an undo.

Gates (local): lint 0 errors, test:ci 1300, build.
